headline: Oil Prices Hold Steady as Supply Surplus Concerns Offset Geopolitical Risk
summary: Brent crude futures traded up 17 cents at $92.12 a barrel as rising expectations for a supply surplus and higher interest rates were counterbalanced by shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
why: Crude oil is a primary global commodity input whose price directly influences energy sector equities, inflation expectations, and transportation costs worldwide.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: Direct market pricing for Brent crude oil futures.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Persistent supply surplus expectations and higher interest rate sentiments were offset by ongoing shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving prices largely steady.
